title: The Hand Upon the Wall
old_p1: King Belshazzar had a great feast, a big party. Suddenly the fingers of a man’s hand appeared and wrote on the wall! No wise man could read it, and the king was afraid.
Then the queen remembered Daniel, a man with an excellent spirit, wise and good. “Send for Daniel,” she said. “He can tell you what it means.”
old_p2: The king promised Daniel a fine robe, a gold chain, and a high place in his kingdom if he could read it.
“Keep your gifts,” Daniel said. “I will read the writing anyway.” Daniel told the king the truth, even though it was hard to hear.
Daniel did not tell the truth to get a prize. He told it because it was right. Feel how light your heart is when you are honest.
p1: King Belshazzar had a big party. Then the fingers of a hand wrote words on the wall! The king was afraid.
No wise man could read them. The queen remembered Daniel. “Send for Daniel,” she said. “He can tell you what it means.”
The king promised Daniel gifts for reading it. He would get a red robe, a gold necklace, and a big job.
p2: Daniel said, “Keep your gifts. I will read the writing for you anyway.” Then he told what the words meant. It was not happy news, but Daniel told the truth.
Daniel told the truth because it was right, not to get a prize. You can be truthful too, even when it is hard. Tonight, feel how light an honest heart is.
